solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rover knocking back pint, perhaps, during game, informally

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the span of the other

parts.note: footer is a casual British name for football

indicators.note: knocking back a drink suggests tipping it the other way, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a pint is typically of beer, so beer is the example's class

explanation.surface: A wanderer downs a pint while watching the football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' suggests a dog or a car, but here it is a roving pirate; 'pint, perhaps' is a pint of beer, given backwards and placed inside the slang game word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover in the old sense is a pirate, and a freebooter is a plundering pirate too.

clue.text: Stable establishment

explanation.surface: A horse yard described as a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steady as an adjective and a business house as a noun, two separate senses.

clue.text: See eager sailor painting yacht first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every one of the following words

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic seaman is busy painting his yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, an old-fashioned verb for seeing.

clue.text: Bachelor requesting quiet on vessel, seeing creature of the deep

parts.note: requesting means asking
sh is the call for quiet
an ark is a vessel, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: A single man asks for silence aboard a boat when he spots a sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' places SH above ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: The basking shark is a huge plankton-feeding fish, an inhabitant of the ocean.

clue.text: Extravagant? Not in an army corps

parts.note: not in means out
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Is it too much to be outside the army corps?
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional or bizarre, so beyond normal bounds, which is how extravagant is meant.

clue.text: Creature that burrows, destroying the marrow

indicators.note: destroying the following words wrecks their order so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden pest ruins a prize vegetable by tunnelling into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms tunnel through soil, so they are the textbook animal that digs.

clue.text: Mop Cornish sailor used?

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Is this the mop a Cornish seaman used?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that SW is a stretch for 'Cornish'; it also hints that a swab is just what a sailor would use on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab is a mop for cleaning a ship's deck, and to swab is to mop.

clue.text: Recoil, but ultimately accept coarse cotton fabric

parts.note: to recoil is to wince
yet and but are both conjunctions meaning however

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end letter of each of the two words after it

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at a scratchy material, yet takes it in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse' looks like part of the fabric's description, but it only gives its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Winceyette is a brushed cotton cloth often used for nightwear.

clue.text: Popular book in French is small, digested by beauty, 21

indicators.note: digested by places the earlier pieces inside the stomach of the following word

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
est is the French word for is
21-down is RIGHT, abbreviated to R

explanation.surface: A hit novel is said to be small in French, yet swallowed by a beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' refers to the answer to 21-down, RIGHT, used here in its abbreviated form R.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestseller is a book with very large sales, i.e. a popular one.

clue.text: Merchandise finally put in place in an Irishman's warehouse

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the name that follows

parts.note: Rory is a typical Irish man's name

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: to posit is literally to put in place, from Latin ponere

explanation.surface: Goods end up stored in an Irishman's depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where things are stored, as a warehouse is.

clue.text: Working American's responsibility

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American employee's duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' as a link, so 'American has responsibility'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty, the obligation one bears.

clue.text: Absorption transforming a Latin mission endlessly

indicators.note: transforming changes the form of the letters, so they are rearranged
endlessly removes the last letter from the word it follows

explanation.surface: Absorption of the culture changes a Latin missionary venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes N off MISSION, leaving MISSIO, which joins A and LATIN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Assimilation is the process of taking something in and incorporating it, as absorption does.

clue.text: Team-beater's hairy facial growth

parts.note: a side is a team
a whisk beats eggs, so a whisker is one who beats, and the 's makes it possessive

explanation.surface: The man who beat the team sports bushy whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as SIDE + WHISKER'S: the 'beater' is a whisker, one who whisks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidewhiskers are hair grown down the cheeks beside the ears, also called sideburns.

clue.text: Doubts young woman revealed about donating

indicators.note: about places the first piece around the second

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman
donating means giving

explanation.surface: A girl admits to second thoughts about her charitable giving.
explanation.definitionFit: Misgivings are feelings of doubt or apprehension.

clue.text: Craftswoman's burden, securing copper disc

indicators.note: securing holds the following pieces inside the word before it

parts.note: stress is a burden or strain
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
an LP is a long-playing record, a disc

explanation.surface: A woman artisan's stress over holding on to a copper disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptress is a female sculptor, a woman who works in a craft of carving or modelling.

clue.text: Humble worker in pub, taking it over under a false name

indicators.note: in sets the worker within the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a cog in the machine is a lowly worker
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A lowly worker in a pub takes over under an assumed identity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is not a reversal signal here: it is O, as on a cricket scorecard, added after IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito describes someone concealing their identity, using an alias rather than their real name.

clue.text: Encouragement given by nice vet in novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take on a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasant vet in a book offers some motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that motivates or spurs someone on.

clue.text: Leader of infantry escorted back, carrying a standard

indicators.note: leader of asks for the opening letter of the next word
carrying has the reversed word bearing the A inside it
back sends the word for escorted the other way

parts.note: to escort is to lead, so escorted is led

explanation.surface: An infantry commander, escorted to the rear, bears a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LED into DEL, which holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a model of perfection, a standard to aim at.

clue.text: Aussie screecher giving girl a headache initially

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A noisy Australian gives a woman a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: The galah is an Australian cockatoo known for its raucous shrieking call.

clue.text: Dedicated duke eclipsed by English management group

indicators.note: eclipsed by says one letter is blotted out and outshone by another in its place

parts.note: dedicated means committed

explanation.surface: A devoted aristocrat is overshadowed by an Englishman on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee is a body of people appointed to run or oversee affairs.

clue.text: Long-time heretic, one replacing a surgeon

indicators.note: replacing says the numeral one takes the place of the letter a

parts.note: a veteran has served a long time
an Arian followed Arius, condemned as a heretic
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lifelong heretic stands in for a surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Arius was a 4th-century priest whose teaching was condemned; 'surgeon' is fair because vets operate on animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A veterinarian, or vet, is an animal doctor who performs operations on animals.

clue.text: Authority to produce script for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners means the word is as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: to produce script is to write

explanation.surface: Permission to write a play to be broadcast on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A right is an entitlement or authority to do something.

clue.text: Long garment gnome shortened

indicators.note: shortened cuts the end letter off the word for gnome

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying, a maxim

explanation.surface: A garden gnome's long coat has been taken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' is not the garden figure but a gnome in its sense of an aphorism.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is an ankle-length skirt, dress or coat.

clue.text: Pretext contributing to extensive ill-feeling

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An excuse that adds to widespread resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil, figuratively, is a cover or disguise, so a pretext concealing real motives.

clue.text: Compulsion to work and press together when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking points to the spoken form of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: to knead is to work dough, pressing and folding it

explanation.surface: An urge to work and squeeze things together while talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is a necessity or obligation, a compelling requirement.

clue.text: Greek character left? Terrible time for a crusade!

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
grim means terrible or dreadful
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A Greek on the left complains of an awful time on crusade.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade was originally a journey to the Holy Land, as a religious pilgrimage also is.

clue.text: A couple of notes of little distinction

parts.note: the first of a couple of notes: so (or soh) of the sol-fa scale
the second of the couple, so again

explanation.surface: Just two musical notes make an unremarkable tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple of notes' is the sol-fa note so given twice; the two halves are shown as one note each.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling or mediocre, not special in any way.

clue.text: Name Alice's illustrator talked of after church anniversary

indicators.note: after puts the name and the illustrator behind the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: talked of means the illustrator's surname as spoken

parts.note: Sir John Tenniel drew the original illustrations for Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: The name of Alice's illustrator comes up at a church anniversary.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are given out of order: CE comes first, then N, then a sound-alike of TENNIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A centennial is a hundredth anniversary, a centenary.
